questions.stem: A coin is flipped $200$ times and lands on heads $118$ times. What is the experimental probability (relative frequency) of heads?
questions.explanation: Experimental probability $= \frac{\text{number of times event occurs}}{\text{total trials}} = \frac{118}{200} = 0.59$.

questions.stem: As the number of trials increases, what happens to the experimental probability?

options.text: It always equals the theoretical probability
It moves further from the theoretical probability
It tends to get closer to the theoretical probability

questions.explanation: As the number of trials increases, the experimental probability (relative frequency) tends to settle down and get closer to the theoretical probability. This is sometimes called the law of large numbers.
